$comment: P6a org.policy.manage exclusively gates org credentials and agent policy for live owners/admins; it grants no Host-global secret or operator authority. Single-user Hosts refuse these new org commands. Multi-tenant Host surface policy (docs/plans/2026-10-20-multi-user-organizations-permissions-and-rollout.md §8). Maps every CommandDescriptor capability in protocol/companion-commands.json to the collaboration action a tenant principal must hold before the Host dispatches the command. A test fails when the manifest gains a capability this file does not classify; an unclassified capability is denied in multi-tenant mode. Single-user mode skips Host standing checks; executionCapabilities and executionCommands still apply when execution is explicitly disabled. Actions come from protocol/collab-capabilities-v1.json. commandOverrides correct capability-level client standing for Host-global arms; client is not a claim about where code executes. Stream adapters have explicit execution flags when no descriptor exists. P5 routes host-data to an OIDC-bound person brain only when a server fleet is installed; personModelCommands label the P6 model-access dormancy. personHostStateCommands apply only to tenant devices on multi-tenant Hosts with a person fleet, using client.read/client.write and the partition intent policy. Message data arms are storage-only; agent replies remain refused.

classes.client: Client-local bridge plumbing; no additional Host standing check. Host-stored data uses host-data instead.
classes.host-data: Person-partitioned data on multi-tenant cognia-server: OIDC-bound person and live non-guest org standing; no workspace. No installed fleet: 403 host_data_unpartitioned. Message arms store/read history only; agent replies stay execution_isolation_unavailable. Single-user unchanged.
classes.operator-only: Never served to a tenant principal in multi-tenant mode.
classes.org-action: Requires the named org-scope action for the tenant org.
classes.workspace-action: Requires the named workspace-scope action in the workspace the Host resolves for the target (never a renderer-supplied id). When the Host cannot resolve a workspace, the fallback org action applies.
classes.sandboxed-execution: Requires execution.request in the resolved workspace AND a sandbox placement; never a host process.
